title: Prompt
description: The canonical, model-agnostic generation request. This is the artifact of record for what the generator is asked to produce: the audio is a build product derived from it. It is not a string. It is a pure function of the RequirementSpec, the Composition and the Lyrics, plus the target adapter, and it is rendered into a target-specific form (for example rendered/ace_step_1_5.json) rather than written by hand. Canonicalisation: keys sorted, numbers formatted with a fixed precision, no insignificant whitespace, so the same intent always yields the same bytes; the manifest records prompt_sha256 over that canonical form. Anything that affected the audio and is not recorded here is not reproducible.

seed.description: The song-level seed. Every stage derives its own seed from this one, so re-running a single stage cannot perturb the others.

style.description: What the song should sound like. Renders into the generator's style/caption prompt.

metadata.description: The numeric and categorical facts of the request. On ACE-Step 1.5 these render into the prompt-level CoT fields, so they are a strong prior and not a guarantee: each one must also be measured on the rendered audio.

form.description: The section plan, referenced from composition.json rather than duplicated, so the two cannot drift.

lyrics.description: A content-addressed reference to the lyric artifact. The prompt carries the hash, not a stale copy.

negative.description: Per-field exclusions mirroring the positive fields. Renders into the generator's negative conditioning, which is a weak lever and never a guarantee on its own.

references.description: Optional external material the generation is conditioned on.

audio.description: Path or handle to reference timbre audio.

melody.description: Path or handle to a melody or MIDI reference.

target.description: Which generator, which weights, which graph, which sampler settings. Model identity is recorded rather than assumed, so 'same model' is provable.

notes.description: Human-readable rationale for each choice, for review. Never sent to the generator.

field.description: Dotted path into this prompt, e.g. 'metadata.bpm'.

requirement_id.description: The RequirementSpec id this choice serves, when there is one.

provenance.description: Where this prompt came from, so it can be regenerated and audited.

Style.description: The descriptive half of the request, produced from a controlled vocabulary of tag bins rather than typed. Selections are stored by option id; the rendered tags and the rendered string are stored alongside so the exact bytes sent to the generator are always recoverable, even if the vocabulary is later reworded. Both go to the generator.

vocabulary_ref.description: Which vocabulary revision produced these tags. Pinning it is what makes an old prompt still render identically after the vocabulary is extended.

selections.description: The bin state, keyed by bin id. This is what a UI binds to and what a saved preset restores.

rendered_tags.description: The tags actually emitted, in canonical render order, after the budget has been applied. This is the tag list the model sees.

rendered_string.description: rendered_tags joined with ', '. Recorded verbatim because it is the exact input to the generator, and because it is the field the human actually reads and reviews.

omitted_tags.description: Tags dropped to respect the tag budget. Recorded so a truncation is visible in the artifact instead of being silently lost.

free_text.description: The residual descriptive clause in natural language, for what the vocabulary cannot hold. Appended after the rendered tags.

dimensions.description: A denormalised view of the selections by axis, generated from the bins. Kept because the compliance battery scores these axes separately and a single tag blob cannot be checked per requirement.

Selection.description: One bin's state. The uniform shape lets the UI, the renderer and the linter all read every bin the same way; which fields are meaningful is declared by the bin's `control` in the vocabulary.

options.description: Selected option ids. Used by every select control, and by numeric_with_descriptor for its word tag.

text.description: For combo_free and any bin that accepts typed input.

Metadata.description: The exactly-checkable half of the request. Every field here has a corresponding measurement on the rendered audio; the value recorded here is what was asked for, not what was produced.

duration_s.description: ACE-Step 1.5 supports 10 s to 600 s; the adapter must reject or route outside that.

language.description: ISO 639-1 code, restricted to the target's supported set at render time.

Form.description: A reference to the section plan in composition.json, not a copy. The composer owns the structure; the prompt points at it.

sections.description: Denormalised view for the renderer and for human review. Generated from composition.json; never edited by hand.

label.description: The tag written into the lyric text, e.g. '[Verse 1]'.

sha256.description: Content hash, so the prompt cannot silently refer to a lyric that has since changed.

section_tags.description: Whether the rendered lyric text carries [Verse]/[Chorus] tags. ACE-Step uses them for structure.

metrical.description: Derived per-line syllable and stress data, computed in code. Present because the melody and the prompt both depend on it; never produced by the oracle.

Negative.description: What to avoid. Each field mirrors a positive field. Negative conditioning is a weak lever: it biases away, it does not exclude, so a requirement expressed only here is not enforced by it.

artist_references.description: Named artists whose style must not be imitated. Recorded here so the render and the compliance report can both prove what was excluded; the policy check is a separate oracle question.

Target.description: Everything needed to reproduce the render, including the parts a human would otherwise remember: the graph and the sampler settings.

weights_sha256.description: Content hash per weight file. Optional because hashing multi-gigabyte files is slow; when present it makes 'same model' provable rather than declared.

graph_ref.description: For a graph runner, the workflow that was executed, e.g. the packaged audio_ace_step1_5_xl_turbo template.

sampler.description: Diffusion sampler settings: steps, cfg, sampler name, scheduler, denoise.

lm.description: Language-model settings that generate audio codes (generate_audio_codes, cfg_scale, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p). Distinct from the diffusion sampler and must not be conflated with it.

batch_size.description: Best-of-N is native on ACE-Step 1.5; the batch that was rendered is recorded here.

candidate_index.description: Which candidate of the batch this artifact is, so a specific render is addressable.

built_at.description: ISO 8601. Recorded but excluded from the canonical form used for hashing.

builder.description: Tool and version that built this prompt.
